question: As per the Transparency International report released in February 2025, what was India’s rank in the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**96**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Transparency International** released the **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) 2024** in **February 2025**, providing a global snapshot of public sector corruption.
 
• In the **2024** rankings, **India** was placed at the **96th** position among **180 countries** and territories.
 
• India’s overall score in **2024** was **39** on a scale where **0** is "highly corrupt" and **100** is "very clean."
 
• Compared to the previous year's report (**CPI 2023**), where India held the **93rd** rank, the country has seen a slight decline in its standing by three positions.
 
• The report highlights that India’s score has shown fluctuations but remains below the global average, reflecting ongoing challenges in curbing **public sector corruption** and ensuring **transparency**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 96**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Transparency International:**
 
 
• It is an international **non-governmental organization** founded in **1993**.
 
• The organization is headquartered in **Berlin, Germany**, and operates in more than **100 countries**.
 
• It is primarily known for the **Corruption Perceptions Index**, the **Global Corruption Barometer**, and the **Bribe Payers Index**.
 
 
 
• **Scoring and Ranking Mechanism:**
 
 
• The **CPI** uses **13** different data sources from **12** independent institutions to aggregate perceptions of corruption.
 
• These institutions include the **World Bank**, the **World Economic Forum**, and the **Economist Intelligence Unit**.
 
• A country's rank indicates its position relative to other countries in the index, while its **score** indicates the perceived level of corruption.
 
 
 
• **Global Performance in 2024:**
 
 
• **Denmark** topped the index once again with a score of **90**, followed by **Finland** and **New Zealand**.
 
• At the opposite end of the spectrum, **Somalia**, **Syria**, and **South Sudan** were ranked at the bottom of the list.
 
• The **global average score** for the **2024** index remained stagnant at **43**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **South Asian Comparison:**
 
 
• Among its neighbors, **Bhutan** continues to perform exceptionally well, ranking **26th** with a score of **68**.
 
• **Pakistan** was ranked lower at **133rd**, while **Bangladesh** was positioned at **149th** in the **2024** report.
 
• **India** shares the **96th** rank with countries like the **Maldives**.
 
 
 
• **Implications for India:**
 
 
• The **96th rank** suggests a need for stronger **anti-corruption laws**, better **whistleblower protection**, and enhanced **institutional independence**.
 
• Corruption levels often impact **foreign direct investment (FDI)** and the overall **ease of doing business** in a nation.
 
• The **2024 report** emphasizes that countries with weak **justice systems** tend to struggle more with systemic corruption.
 
 

4d
